edits.old: Classic and SBE plan-cache reuse have different structural constraints: classic stores index-assignment information and reconstructs bounds and the plan for the incoming query, whereas the SBE cache stores a reusable execution tree. The $in regression test explains that classic applies explode-for-sort after cache retrieval. (high confidence)
edits.new: Classic and SBE plan-cache reuse have different structural constraints: the classic cache maps a generously parameterized query shape to a description of which index(es) to use and, on a hit, a new query execution tree is built for the incoming query, whereas the SBE cache maps a more conservatively parameterized shape to an actual SBE plan that can be cloned and run. The $in regression test explains that classic applies explode-for-sort after retrieving from the plan cache. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89436 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/jstests/core/query/plan_cache/in_expression_plan_cache.js

A new query execution tree is built, and the query is run.
The SBE plan cache maps a more conservatively parameterized query shape to a an actual SBE plan which can be cloned and then run.

edits.old: SERVER-66459 documented a correctness failure: sort expansion discarded IETs, so downstream code embedded fixed KeyString bounds and cached reuse with new literals could omit matching documents. SERVER-67576 describes initially excluding these plans from caching before restoring safe support. These are historical defects, not evidence that every current sorted $in query is wrong. (high confidence)
edits.new: SERVER-66459 documented a correctness failure: explode-for-sort discarded the IETs attached to the original IndexScanNode, so downstream code embedded fixed KeyString bounds and cached reuse with different constants could give incorrect or missing results. SERVER-67576 states that SERVER-66459 planned a quick fix of prohibiting explode-for-sort query solutions from being cached, and that SERVER-67576's own work was to re-enable the SBE plan cache in combination with explode for sort. These are historical defects, not evidence that every current sorted $in query is wrong. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-66459 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-67576

edits.old: Structural compatibility does not guarantee that one cached access path remains efficient for all parameter values. The Sydney researchers vary predicate selectivity to study plan choices, and Percona describes uneven indexed-value distributions as a cause of unstable cached-plan performance. (medium confidence)
edits.new: The Sydney researchers vary predicate selectivity (with two-range-predicate queries of controlled selectivity) to study which plan MongoDB chooses. Percona says that if data distribution changes without being bad enough to trigger replanning, MongoDB keeps using the cached plan, which may no longer be the best one, and that unstable data distribution or low-selectivity indexes can cause re-planning loops with degraded performance. Sources: https://15799.courses.cs.cmu.edu/spring2025/papers/23-mongodb/tao-adc2024.pdf ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/

edits.old: On the SBE plan-cache path, eligible filter constants receive parameter IDs and runtime slots. IETs reconstruct index bounds from the incoming parameter-to-expression mapping instead of freezing the first query's literal bounds. (high confidence)
edits.new: With SBE auto-parameterization, auto-parameterized plans read constants from the RuntimeEnvironment instead of inlined constants. When an auto-parameterized predicate becomes index bounds, the IndexBoundsBuilder records it in an IntervalEvaluationTree (IET), which allows the index bounds to be recomputed when the plan is bound to new parameter values. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-66459 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-73589
